chunks: And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked him about a man who has been prevented from his wife, such that he is unable to have intercourse with her. He said:

If he is unable to have intercourse with other women besides her, then he should not keep her unless she is content with that. But if he is able to have intercourse with other women, then there is no harm in his keeping her.

key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: women other than his wife, used for comparison in the ruling
key_terms.بِإِمْسَاكِهَا: in keeping her as his wife
key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man, the subject of the legal ruling
key_terms.عَمَّارٌ السَّابَاطِيُّ: Ammar al-Sabati, the narrator asking the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicates permissibility

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband who cannot have intercourse with his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a husband who is unable to have intercourse with his wife. If his incapacity is general, he should not keep her unless she accepts that situation; but if the problem is specific to her, there is no harm in maintaining the marriage.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4897 - Ammar Al-Sabati asked Imam Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who becomes unable to have intercourse with his wife.
Imam (as) replied: "

If he is also unable to have intercourse with any other woman, then he should not keep her unless she is content with that. However, if he is able to have intercourse with other women, then there is no harm in him keeping her as his wife."
